subject: physics
question_text: Name the processes that make up the cycle of a Carnot engine.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 16 (printed p.125). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the Carnot cycle is isothermal expansion at T₁, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression at T₂, adiabatic compression, in that order, and the last step returns the gas to its starting state.

steps.label: Expansion processes

steps.margin_note: Both expansion steps, named and in order, are the first mark.
steps.why: The two expansion steps take the gas from the source temperature down to the sink temperature, in that order, before the compression half returns it.
common_mistakes: Starting the cycle with an adiabatic step. The cycle begins with the isothermal expansion at T₁.
Saying the temperature changes during the isothermal expansion. It changes only on the adiabatic step.
steps.memory_tip: Expand twice: isothermal first, then adiabatic.

steps.label: Compression processes
lines: the gas rejects heat as it is
is exchanged; the gas warms back
The gas returns to its starting
steps.margin_note: Both compression steps, named and in order, plus the closed cycle, are the second mark.
steps.why: The two compression steps mirror the expansion steps and bring the gas back to T₁ at its original pressure and volume, which is what makes the process a closed cycle.
common_mistakes: Omitting that the cycle closes — the last step must return the gas to its exact starting state.
Saying the gas rejects heat during the adiabatic compression. Heat is rejected on the isothermal step; the adiabatic step exchanges none.
steps.memory_tip: Compress twice: isothermal first, then adiabatic, back to the start.

insider_note: List all four steps in order — isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression, adiabatic compression — and say the cycle returns to its starting state.
